item.title: Personalised GPT News — 16 August 2026
item.description:
Fresh developments include new cancer and Alzheimer’s approvals, concrete Australian digital-policy changes, a new federally supervised crypto bank, and several consumer-facing technology and payment shifts.

  1. FDA approves a new oral multiple-myeloma treatment. On 13 August, the US FDA approved Bristol Myers Squibb’s Zenbexus (iberdomide) with Darzalex and dexamethasone for relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma. The accelerated approval is based on late-stage data and requires confirmatory clinical benefit. Source — Reuters, 13 Aug 2026.
  2. FDA approves a new tau PET imaging agent for Alzheimer’s assessment. On 14 August, Lantheus said the FDA approved Tauklarify, a radioactive PET imaging agent that makes abnormal tau deposits visible in cognitively impaired adults being assessed for Alzheimer’s disease. Source — Reuters, 14 Aug 2026.
  3. (Crypto & finances) World Liberty Financial receives conditional US national trust-bank approval. On 14 August, the US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency conditionally approved a national trust-bank charter for World Liberty Financial, allowing the firm to expand federally supervised stablecoin and custody activities subject to stated conditions. Source — Reuters, 14 Aug 2026.
  4. (Australia) Australia introduces revised legislation requiring large digital platforms to strike more local-news payment deals. On 12 August, Australia introduced a revised media-licensing bill requiring covered platforms to strike deals with at least eight local media companies, with a levy liability equal to 2.5% of Australian advertising revenue and 5% of collected funds allocated to Australian Associated Press. Source — Reuters, 12 Aug 2026.
  5. (Travel) The US made its visa-bond programme permanent for applicants from 50 countries. In August, the US State Department made permanent a programme allowing consular officers to require refundable tourist or business visa bonds of up to US$20,000 from applicants in designated countries; the current list covers 50 countries and can be expanded with notice. Source — Reuters, 12 Aug 2026.
  6. (Privacy) Australia’s Origin Energy disclosed a potential customer-data security incident. On 22 July, Origin Energy said it was investigating possible unauthorised access to some customer data. It said it did not expect affected data to include customer credit-card or bank details and notified Australian cyber, police and privacy authorities. Source — Reuters via Yahoo, 22 Jul 2026.
  7. (Australia) Australia announced a central government Office of AI and planned data-centre resource rules. On 14 July, Australia announced an Office of AI within the Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet. The government also said planned legislation would set rules for large data centres, including limits on water use and a requirement to be net producers of energy. Source — Reuters, 14 Jul 2026.
  8. FDA approves Replimune’s tumour-injected melanoma therapy after earlier rejections. On 6 August, the FDA approved Tudriqev (RP1) with Opdivo for advanced melanoma after prior treatment failure. RP1 is a genetically modified herpes virus injected directly into tumours; confirmatory Phase III work remains under way. Source — Reuters, 6 Aug 2026.
  9. Merck’s first-in-class oral PCSK9 cholesterol drug was approved. On 16 July, the FDA approved Merck’s Lipfendra (enlicitide), the first oral treatment in the PCSK9-inhibitor class. Trials reported LDL reductions of nearly 60% with once-daily dosing. Source — Reuters, 16 Jul 2026.
  10. Lilly reported additional Phase III retatrutide obesity results and set a Q1 2027 FDA filing target. On 23 July, Lilly reported two more late-stage trials of retatrutide. In an 80-week study of adults with severe obesity and heart disease, the highest dose produced average weight loss of 22.6%; in another trial involving obesity and type 2 diabetes, average weight loss reached 20.8%. Source — Reuters, 23 Jul 2026.
  11. A registrational rectal-cancer study reported sustained complete clinical responses with dostarlimab. On 13 July, GSK said the Phase II AZUR-1 trial of Jemperli (dostarlimab) in dMMR/MSI-H locally advanced rectal cancer met its primary objective, with a clinically meaningful rate of participants showing no detectable cancer at 12 months or longer after treatment. Source — GSK regulatory announcement via Reuters/TradingView, 13 Jul 2026.
  12. FDA approves GSK’s targeted drug for previously treated ROS1-positive lung cancer. On 22 July, GSK announced FDA approval of Jideytro (zidesamtinib) for adults with locally advanced or metastatic ROS1-positive non-small cell lung cancer previously treated with a ROS1 kinase inhibitor. Source — GSK regulatory announcement via Reuters/TradingView, 22 Jul 2026.
  13. FDA approves a wearable injector version of Sanofi’s Sarclisa. On 10 July, the FDA approved Sarclisa Escena, allowing the multiple-myeloma drug to be delivered under the skin through an on-body wearable injector rather than only by intravenous infusion. Source — Reuters via Investing.com, 10 Jul 2026.
  14. Biogen’s anti-tau Alzheimer’s drug reduced tau substantially in a mid-stage trial, despite missing its dose-response primary endpoint. On 14 July, researchers reported that diranersen reduced tau by roughly 50% to 65% across studied doses. The lowest dose also showed slower cognitive decline on five of six assessment tools; Biogen plans a pivotal Phase III trial in 2027. Source — Reuters, 14 Jul 2026.
  15. Google was ordered to open Android functions and some anonymised search-optimisation data to qualifying rivals in the EU. On 16 July, the European Commission specified Digital Markets Act measures requiring Google to open 11 Android functions to rival AI assistants from July 2027 and to share qualifying anonymised search-optimisation data with competing search/AI services from January 2027, subject to security and privacy checks. Source — Reuters, 16 Jul 2026.
  16. (Privacy) EU lawmakers backed temporary child-abuse detection rules while exempting end-to-end encrypted communications. On 9 July, EU lawmakers backed reinstating temporary online child-sexual-abuse detection rules but voted to exempt end-to-end encrypted communications such as WhatsApp, Telegram and Signal from the interim scanning regime. Source — Reuters via Investing.com, 9 Jul 2026.
  17. (Privacy) EU regulators told Meta to change addictive Facebook and Instagram design features or risk fines. On 10 July, the European Commission issued preliminary findings that Meta had not adequately addressed risks linked to highly personalised recommendations, autoplay and infinite scroll under the Digital Services Act, and demanded changes or the company could face penalties. Source — Reuters via MarketScreener, 10 Jul 2026.
  18. ChatGPT Work and GPT-5.6 launched publicly. On 9 July, OpenAI launched ChatGPT Work, combining ChatGPT with Codex-style agentic capabilities for producing documents, presentations, websites and other multi-step work, alongside the GPT-5.6 model family. Source — Reuters via Investing.com, 9 Jul 2026.
  19. The ECB selected 36 payment providers for the digital-euro pilot. On 14 July, the European Central Bank selected 36 banks and payment providers, including Deutsche Bank, UniCredit and Revolut, for a 12-month pilot scheduled to begin in the second half of 2027. The beta transactions will test technical and user-interface functions but will not yet constitute legal tender. Source — Reuters, 14 Jul 2026.
  20. Samsung launched its first US co-branded credit card, fully integrated with Samsung Wallet. On 20 July, Samsung and Barclays launched the Galaxy Card on Visa’s network. Users can apply, manage the account, track spending and redeem rewards through Samsung Wallet, with 5% cash back on Samsung purchases. Source — Reuters, 20 Jul 2026.
